correction.text: upper Sindh, the part of Sind north of about 26 N

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. "Subahdar of upper Sindh" by Mughal decree; the page gives no extent. Upper Sindh is north of about 26 N (about 59,000 km2).

New keyframe: independent from 1736 ("Declared as an Independent State by Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah in 1736"); "most of Sindh" under the Kalhoras (a son was subahdar of Sehwan). The page dates the spread over Sindh to no year, so the whole of Sindh is drawn from 1736 (about 142,130 km2; no infobox area). Sind became a Durrani vassal in 1748-1750 without losing the shape; Nader Shah's invasion (1739) is recorded in the wars. Repair 2026-10-25: the "northern half of Kutch district" that this shape first carried is taken out. It was drawn as the gazetteer's Kutch north of 23.4 N and so lay on the mainland of cutch-state (9,100 km2, 36 cells, 1736-1783) with no event in either dossier. The Kalhora page dates that holding to no year; the only dated evidence is the Cutch State page (Ghulam Shah Kalhoro's attacks of 1763-64 and 1765, the territories he conquered returned after the 1770 marriage), so the Kutch land is drawn as an occupation 1765-1770 in the ledger and not as a permanent part of the shape.

region.text: upper Sindh, the part of Sind north of about 26 N

ledger.note: 1701: Yar Muhammad Kalhoro is made subahdar of upper Sindh. Infobox "Established: 1701"; "was made subahdar of upper Sindh by royal decree of the Mughals" (no year or month for the decree).

1736: bridging, page silent on the acquisitions. "Declared as an Independent State by Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah in 1736"; his son was "appointed subahdar of Sehwan, overseeing most of Sindh"; none of the conquests is dated on the Kalhora page. The Noor Mohammad Kalhoro page (read in the repair of 2026-10-25) lists them without years: Thatta taken from the Mughal governor Naib Muhammad Sadiq, "subjugating Bakhar Sarkar (Northern Sindh), Sehwan Sarkar (Central Sindh)", Shikarpur taken from the Daudpotras, the Sibi and Kachhi plains, Shahbandar from the Jams of Kakrala; it puts the title Nawab Khuda-Yar Khan and the title Kalhora Nawab of Sindh in 1737 "after taking Thatta", so lower Sindh was held by 1737 at the latest. The year stays the Kalhora page's 1736 (confidence 1). Repair 2026-10-25: the northern half of Kutch district is no longer part of this gain (see the occupation of 1765-1770).

ledger.note: 1765: Ghulam Shah Kalhoro holds the conquered Kutch territories. The Cutch State page: under Rao Godji II (1761-1778) the state "faced its biggest defeat at hands of Mian Ghulam Shah Kalhoro of Sindh", who attacked twice, in 1763-64 (a battle near Jara) and again in 1765, and Godji "had to make a truce with him after losing several territories"; the Kalhora page has "The northern half of Kutch district was also under the Kalhora Dynasty" (undated). The pages do not date the loss of any town, so the start is bridged to the second attack of 1765 (confidence 1), and the region is the Kalhora page's phrase drawn over the Cutch mainland; Cutch keeps its state, hence an occupation and not a gain. cutch-state does not yet carry the matching occupation (its wars list the Kalhora attacks).
1768: the court moves from Khudabad to Hyderabad. "Hyderabad: from 1768 (text), until 1783 (infobox)."

ledger.note: 1770: Ghulam Shah Kalhoro returns the towns to the Rao of Cutch. The Cutch State page: after the 1770 marriage of a daughter of Wesuji to the Mian, "the towns of Busta Bandar and Lakhpat and others territories that had been conquered by the Mián Kalhoro" were returned; the page gives no separate year for the handover, so 1770 is the marriage year (confidence 2). Ghulam Shah reigned 1758-1772 (Kalhora page table).

1783: the Talpurs overthrow the Kalhoras at Halani. "established by Mir Fateh Ali Khan in 1783, after he overthrew the Kalhora dynasty in the Battle of Halani"; the Kalhora page: Abdul Nabi Kalhoro "was overthrown in 1783".
1783: the Kalhora dynasty ends with Abdul Nabi Kalhoro. His successors were overthrown "at the Battle of Halani".

wars.name: Nader Shah's invasion of India
wars.outcome: "in 1739, during Nader Shah's invasion of India, Mian fled to Umerkot for shelter but was captured by the King of Iran" (Noor Mohammad Kalhoro page); the Kalhora page says the dynasty "succumbed to the invasion of Nader Shah" (undated). No cession, tribute or occupation of Sindh is on any page opened.
wars.note: The Nader Shah's invasion of India page has "all lands west of the Indus river" annexed in 1738-1739 and the lands east of the Indus given back to Muhammad Shah on 16 May 1739, and, undated, "The Governor of Sindh did not comply with Nader Shah's demands"; it does not say which side of the Indus Sindh fell on, so no loss is recorded in the ledger.

wars.name: Durrani conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: Ahmad Shah Durrani conquered Sind "in 1748-1750" and made it a vassal of the Durrani Empire; the page gives no tribute figure and no territorial loss.
wars.note: The page also says Nader Shah's invasion was succumbed to, with no year.

notes: Two pages opened in the first pass (Kalhora dynasty, Talpur dynasty) and three in the repair of 2026-10-25 (Cutch State, Noor Mohammad Kalhoro, Nader Shah's invasion of India; the titles Noor_Muhammad_Kalhoro and Nader_Shah's_invasion_of_the_Mughal_Empire returned url_not_found). The Kalhora page has no area, no Nader Shah year, no Shikarpur, Multan or Kalat. The Durrani vassalage of 1748-1750 is for durrani-empire (ia-03) to record as a vassal_start with counterpart kalhora-dynasty (the page: Sind became "a vassal of the Durrani Empire"); the Mughal grant and the 1736 independence are for mughal-empire (sa-05-a). The Layyah and Bhakkar governorship of 1787-1790 and the jagir cancellation of 1793 are post-dynasty. The page contradicts itself on Abdul Nabi (reign to 1782/1783 but active 1787-93). Gazetteer: Khudabad is not a place; coordinates used. REPAIR 2026-10-25 (review sa-05-x, verdict fail). (a) The permanent shape no longer carries the "northern half of Kutch district": drawn as the gazetteer's Kutch north of 23.4 N it covered 36 cells (about 9,100 km2) of cutch-state's mainland for 1736-1783 with no event in either dossier. The reviewer offered three ways out: limit it to the Great Rann, drop it, or add a loss/gain pair to both dossiers if a page shows Kalhora rule on the mainland. The Cutch State page does (Lakhpat, Busta Bandar and other conquests of 1763-65, returned after the 1770 marriage), but as a conquest later handed back by a ruler whose state went on, so it is an occupation (occupation_start 1765, confidence 1; occupation_end 1770, confidence 2) over the northern half of the Cutch mainland and Lakhpat, drawn only for those years; the Great Rann alone would have been an empty claim. I did not touch cutch-state (verdict pass): it needs the matching occupation_start and occupation_end with counterpart kalhora-dynasty, 1765 and 1770; its wars already list the Kalhora attacks. Busta Bandar and Lakhpat are not in the gazetteer (Lakhpat is a 25 km circle at 68.78 E, 23.82 N). (b) Thin items tried: the Noor Mohammad Kalhoro page lists the conquests of Sindh (Thatta, Bakhar and Sehwan sarkars, Shikarpur, Sibi, Kachhi) without a year and puts the Nawab title in 1737 against 1736 on the Kalhora page, so the all-Sindh gain stays at 1736, confidence 1. Nader Shah's invasion is now in the wars (1739: Noor Mohammad captured; no land on any page); the Nader Shah's invasion of India page names no Sindh cession, so there is no ledger event. Counterpart still needing a dossier: talpur-dynasty (starts 1783, a Cliopatria row of sa-05).
